rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Thermal radiation** is electromagnetic energy (mainly infrared) emitted by every body above absolute zero — it needs no medium, travels at the speed of light, and splits at a surface into reflected, absorbed and transmitted parts ($r + a + t = 1$). A **perfectly black body** absorbs everything ($a = 1$) and, by Kirchhoff's law, is also the **ideal radiator**: good absorbers are good emitters.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - r + a + t = 1 - E = e σ T⁴ (real body); e = a (Kirchhoff)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Good absorber = good emitter** (Kirchhoff) — a black surface both heats fast and cools fast.  ·  **Radiation needs no medium** — it is the only mode through vacuum.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "All bodies emit thermal radiation at all temperatures above absolute zero."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024*** — blackened utensil bottoms; white summer clothes.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Heat That Crosses Empty Space The Sun's energy crosses 150 million kilometres of vacuum to warm your face. That is radiation: heat carried by electromagnetic waves, needing no medium, travelling at the speed of light, and obeying surface rules — black surfaces absorb and emit best, shiny ones reflect.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2024) ### 2.1 Nature of thermal radiation - Electromagnetic waves (mainly infrared for everyday temperatures) emitted by all bodies above 0 K. - Needs **no material medium** — travels through vacuum at $c = 3\times10^8$ m/s. - Travels in straight lines; can be reflected and refracted like light.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Answer with absorbing power for the pot, reflecting power for the clothes."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short (2m): Why does a thermos flask silver its walls?** — Silvered surfaces have high reflecting power, cutting radiative exchange between the inner and outer walls; the vacuum between already blocks conduction and convection.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Pair this with the Stefan's law question from the same 2024 paper.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Kirchhoff's law links absorption and emission** — the reason colour matters at both ends of heat exchange.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: r + a + t = 1; perfect black body: a = 1; ideal radiator = perfect absorber.  ·  Black utensil bottoms absorb well; white clothes reflect well.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The thermos flask defeats all three modes: vacuum (no conduction/convection) + silvered walls (no radiation).
